malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The backdoor uses DNS TXT records to communicate with its C&C server, sending and receiving commands and data via DNS queries and responses.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely C/C++ or similar, as typical for Windows malware)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code crafts DNS queries with TXT record requests to a C&C-controlled domain, encodes commands/data in the DNS payload, and parses responses to receive instructions, enabling covert command-and-control communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware using DNS for C&C is a known evasion technique, as DNS traffic is often allowed and less scrutinized than HTTP/S.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not use DNS TXT records for command-and-control or data exfiltration; DNS is typically used for domain resolution only.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use DNS TXT records for configuration or service discovery, but not for remote command execution.
key_indicators: Unusual volume of DNS TXT queries to external domains
Parsing and execution of data received in DNS responses
Absence of standard HTTP/S C&C traffic

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via phishing email delivers the Mozart backdoor to the target system.
Backdoor executes and establishes covert C&C channel using DNS TXT records.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can send commands and receive data from the infected system.

behavioral_signatures: Malware establishing C&C via DNS TXT records
Unusual DNS query patterns with encoded payloads
Execution of commands received via DNS
file_indicators: Presence of unknown binaries associated with Mozart backdoor
network_indicators: Frequent DNS TXT queries to attacker-controlled domains
DNS traffic with large or unusual TXT record payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DNS traffic for excessive or anomalous TXT record queries, especially to domains not associated with legitimate services. Correlate with endpoint process activity to identify binaries making such requests. Flag execution of commands or scripts received via DNS responses.
